task_name: Compact filter bar and one-row header on narrow hosts
description: Item 1 (revised design, popover): the filter block is gone from the content column. A 'Filters' chip button sits in RelationshipGraph's header row left of the zoom controls, passed through a new optional `actions` slot (additive; every existing prop kept). Where no graph is drawn (graph missing, no projection yet) the same button sits in a slim right-aligned row of its own. The button (aria-haspopup=dialog, aria-expanded, aria-controls while open) opens FiltersPopover: a non-modal role=dialog labelled 'Graph filters' on the app's menu surface (.menu, --shadow-pop, fixed position right-aligned under the button, clamped to the window), following Menu.tsx's pattern (useEscape layer, capture-phase outside mousedown). It holds Direction and Depth selects, a 'Relationship types · n of N' heading with the labelled kind chips, the symbol-layer reason (only while Defines/Calls are disabled) and 'Reset filters' in a menu footer (only while filters differ from defaults). Changes apply at once; the graph stays visible behind it. Focus moves to the first control on open; Escape or a press outside closes it and puts focus back on the button; the button itself toggles it. While filters differ from defaults the button reads 'Filters · <n>' (n = number of differing settings among direction, depth and types) and takes the pressed chip look (data-changed); its title always states the current settings, e.g. 'Both · 2 steps · 4 of 7 types'. Open/closed is explorer useState (survives tab switches, no history entry). Item 2: inside the existing @container metaproject (max-width: 760px) block the '.flows-heading' is visually hidden with the sr-only declarations (still in the accessibility tree), so the header is one row. Item 3: with the filter block gone and a one-row header, the graph gets the height the 182 px bar and the second header row took; not measured here.

noticed_not_touched.what: The shared icon set has no funnel/filter glyph (only clearFilters, a funnel with an x), so the Filters button uses a trailing chevron instead of a filter icon.

assumptions: 'How many settings differ' counts three settings: direction, depth and the set of relationship types (any difference in types counts once), so the count is 1-3.

The popover is not built on Menu.tsx itself, because Menu closes on every item selection and its items are menuitems; it reuses Menu's surface class (.menu, .menu-header, .menu-footer), positioning, useEscape layer and outside-press handling instead.
A press outside returns focus to the button (as the dispatch says), unlike Menu.tsx, which leaves focus where the press went.

behavior_changes.description: The Filters button text is 'Filters' at the defaults and 'Filters · <n>' when n settings differ, with a trailing chevron; its tooltip always shows the current settings ('Both · 1 step · 5 of 7 types').
alternatives: A leading icon instead of the chevron (needs a new glyph in Icon.tsx)

behavior_changes.description: The popover is 320 px wide, right-aligned with the button and opens below it; inside: Direction and Depth on one row, a 'Relationship types · n of N' heading, the chips, the symbol-layer note, and 'Reset filters' at the bottom right.
alternatives: Reset at the top next to the heading

behavior_changes.description: The popover stays open while the user changes settings (each change applies at once) and stays open across a switch to Wiki and back, because open/closed is explorer state; it is only rendered in Graph mode.
alternatives: Close the popover when the view changes

behavior_changes.description: When no graph is drawn (graph missing or no projection yet), the Filters button sits alone in a slim right-aligned row at the top of the content column.
alternatives: Put the button in the list header instead
